title: Berlin — IHH content reconciliation
header: Private editorial working note, 17 October 2026. **REQUIRES HUMAN SIGN-OFF.** This is not approved visitor copy. No changes to `inductees/berlin/copy.md` are authorized by this note.

IHH starting page: [irving-berlin](https://immigranthallofhonor.org/inductees/inductee-irving-berlin/), retrieved during this review. Line references identify the retrieved text view, not a stable page anchor. Facts are inventoried below in IHH’s order. Compound rows retain all their components; NOT VERIFIED applies to each component unless a narrower status is explicitly stated.
The IHH page and repository manifest were inspected. Existing source records are leads, not fresh confirmation of every IHH statement.

IB: The Irving Berlin Music Company (official estate site), “Irving Berlin – Concise Biography”
KC: Kennedy Center, “On This Day in the Arts: December 3”

evidence: Irving Berlin was born Israel Beilin on May 11, 1888.
L10.note: Every part of the IHH claim appears in the quoted text from The Irving Berlin Music Company (official estate site).

evidence: Irving Berlin was born Israel Beilin on May 11, 1888.
L11.note: No source we checked gives “Israel Berlin”. His estate’s biography gives “Israel Beilin”; Encyclopedia.com and Britannica give “Israel Baline”. “Berlin” was the later stage name. Suggested: “Israel Beilin (also spelled Baline)”. Note for our own profile: it uses “Baline”; consider adding the estate’s spelling.

L12.claim: Born: May 11, 1888, his exact birthplace is unknown, although his family was living in Tolochin, Russia (now Talachyn, Belarus) when they immigrated to New York in 1893
evidence: his exact place of birth is unknown, although his family had been living in Tolochin, Byelorussia, when they immigrated to New York in 1893
L12.note: IHH’s wording closely follows the estate’s official biography. Other reference works give Tyumen (Encyclopedia.com; the Walk of Fame record gives “Temun, Russia”), which is why the birthplace is best left open, as IHH does.

evidence: On September 22, 1989, at the age of 101, Irving Berlin died in his sleep in his town house in New York City.
L13.note: Every part of the IHH claim appears in the quoted text from The Irving Berlin Music Company (official estate site).

L15.note: IHH gives “n/a”; nothing to verify. The sources agree he had little formal schooling.

evidence: He was equally at home writing for Broadway and Hollywood.
L16.note: The estate site describes him as a composer and songwriter throughout.

evidence: he took his oath on February 6, 1918, and became a citizen of the United States
L17.note: Two passages in the same reference compilation give 1918, specifically 6 February 1918, not 1916. Our profile uses 6 February 1918. The naturalization certificate itself has not been examined.

evidence: a catalog that boasted over 1000 songs
L27.note: The Songwriters Hall of Fame says “over 1000 songs”. “More than 1,500” is widely repeated but was not found in the sources checked. Suggested: “Wrote more than 1,000 songs”, unless IHH has a source for 1,500.

L28.claim: Composed for 19 Broadway shows and 18 motion pictures
evidence: He wrote seventeen complete scores for Broadway musicals and revues, and contributed material to six more.
L28.note: The estate counts 17 complete Broadway scores plus material for 6 more shows, which does not match IHH’s “19 Broadway shows”. The film count (18) was not found in these sources.

L29.claim: Co-founded the American Society of Composers, Authors, and Publishers (1914)
evidence: Irving Berlin was a co-founder of ASCAP (American Society of Composers, Authors and Publishers)
L29.note: Co-founder status confirmed by the estate and the Songwriters Hall of Fame. Neither page states ASCAP’s 1914 founding year.

evidence: founder of his own music publishing company
In 1919 he founded his own music publishing company, Irving Berlin, Inc.
opened own publishing firm, Irving Berlin, Inc., 1914
L30.note: He founded his own publishing company; that is confirmed. The year conflicts within Encyclopedia.com (1914 in one entry, 1919 in another), and the company’s exact name at founding is unsettled. Leave the year out until it is checked.

evidence: the Academy Award for Best Song of the Year for "White Christmas" in 1942
L38.note: Precision note: the award was for 1942 and presented at the 1943 ceremony. IHH gives the ceremony year; either year is defensible if labelled.

L39.claim: Army’s Medal of Merit from President Truman (1945)
evidence: the Army's Medal of Merit from President Truman in 1945
L39.note: Every part of the IHH claim appears in the quoted text from The Irving Berlin Music Company (official estate site).

L40.claim: Congressional Gold Medal by President Eisenhower (1955)
evidence: a Congressional Gold Medal for "God Bless America" and other patriotic songs from President Eisenhower in 1955
L40.note: The Songwriters Hall of Fame gives 1955, matching IHH. The estate site gives 1954, probably the act of Congress versus the presentation. Worth labelling.

L41.note: It was a special Tony, not a competitive one.

L42.note: From the Recording Academy’s own list of Lifetime Achievement Award recipients.

L43.claim: Inducted into the Songwriters Hall of Fame (1970
L43.note: Every part of the IHH claim appears in the quoted text from Songwriters Hall of Fame.

L44.claim: Presidential Medal of Freedom from President Ford (1977)
evidence: the Freedom Medal from President Ford in 1977
L44.note: Every part of the IHH claim appears in the quoted text from The Irving Berlin Music Company (official estate site).

L45.note: Tried: the Kennedy Center’s “On This Day: December 3” page (https://www.kennedy-center.org/education/resources-for-educators/classroom-resources/media-and-interactives/artsdays/12-december2/1203/), which confirms the first Honors were held in 1978 but does not list honorees. Neither the estate biography nor the Songwriters Hall of Fame mentions a Kennedy Center Honor. IHH should check this against the Kennedy Center’s honoree list before keeping it.

L46.claim: Star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame (1994)
evidence: Category Recording Address 7095 Hollywood Blvd. Ceremony date 02/01/1994
L46.note: From the Walk of Fame’s own record (Recording category).

L47.claim: The U.S. Army Entertainment Division (AED) named its World Headquarters at Fort Belvoir, Virginia, “The Irving Berlin Center” in his honor (2002)
evidence: In 2002, the U.S. Army at Fort Belvoir, Virginia, named the Army Entertainment Division (AED) World Headquarters "The Irving Berlin Center" in his honor.
L47.note: Every part of the IHH claim appears in the quoted text from The Irving Berlin Music Company (official estate site).

profile_notes: **Birth-name spelling.** The estate’s biography says “Irving Berlin was born Israel Beilin on May 11, 1888.”; Encyclopedia.com says “Born Israel Baline, May 11, 1888” (both read 17 Oct 2026; see row L11). Our `inductees/berlin/copy.md` uses “Baline” only. Not changed; consider giving both spellings.
